summary.en: Hezbollah’s chief is demanding Lebanon free five detained operatives while rejecting any post-UNIFIL force outside U.N. authority, and he asserts that Hezbollah does not work for Iran but that Iran works for Hezbollah. Israeli warplanes are flying intensively at low altitude over southern Lebanon and the Nabatieh region, and Israel is opposing French troop deployment in south Lebanon after the UNIFIL exit. US sanctions on Hezbollah affiliates are reported to have limited impact, and Iran is reported to be developing chemical weapons. The conflict has caused 4,335 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Hezbollah-sjefen krever at Libanon løslater fem fengslede operatører, samtidig som han avviser enhver styrke utenfor FN-myndighet etter UNIFIL, og han påstår at Hezbollah ikke arbeider for Iran, men at Iran arbeider for Hezbollah. Israels krigfly flyr intensivt i lav høyde over Sør-Libanon og Nabatieh-regionen, og Israel motsetter seg fransk tropputplassering i Sør-Libanon etter UNIFIL-avslutning. Amerikanske sanksjoner mot Hezbollah-tilknyttede har ifølge rapporter begrenset effekt, og Iran skal utvikle kjemiske våpen. Konflikten har forårsaket 4 335 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Hezbollah–Israel conflict (2023–present)
background.extract: An ongoing conflict between the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah and Israel began on 8 October 2023, when Hezbollah launched rockets and artillery at Israeli positions following Hamas's October 7 attacks on Israel. The conflict escalated into a prolonged exchange of bombardments, leading to extensive displacement in Israel and Lebanon. The conflict is part of the broader Middle Eastern crisis that began with Hamas's attack, with the short Israeli invasion of Lebanon in 2024 marking the largest escalation of the Hezbollah–Israel conflict since the 2006 Lebanon War. In Arabic, the conflict (2023–2024) is referred to as the "Support War" or the "Gaza Support War."
